controls.title: 3 UNL.SCRMA
controls.description: Supply chain risk management involves implementing a systematic process for managing risk exposures, threats, and vulnerabilities throughout the supply chain. It also involves developing risk response strategies for the risks presented by the supplier, the supplied products and services, or the cyber supply chain.

controls.title: 3.PE P.EM.EDRPR
controls.description: Email domain reputation protections entails monitoring an email domain’s reputation and employing policies to help protect the email domain’s reputation.

controls.title: 3.PEP.DA.ACONT
controls.description: Access control technologies allow an agency to define policies concerning the allowable activities of users and entities to data and resources.

controls.title: 3.PEP.DA.DAUTE
controls.description: This entails identifying agency sensitive data stored, processed, or transmitted, including those located at a service provider and enforcing detailed logging for access or changes to sensitive data.

controls.title: 3.PEP.DA.DINVE
controls.description: Data inventory entails developing, documenting, and maintaining a current inventory of agency data.

controls.title: 3.PEP.DA.DLABE
controls.description: Data labeling is the process of tagging data by categories to protect and control the use of data and identifying a level of risk associated with the data.

controls.title: 3.PEP.DA.DLPRE
controls.description: DLP technologies detect instances of the exfiltration, either malicious or accidental, of agency data.

controls.title: 3.PEP.DA.PDRES
controls.description: Data protection at rest aims to secure data stored on any device or storage medium.

controls.title: 3.PEP.DA.PDTRA
controls.description: Data protection in transit, or data in motion, aims to secure data that is actively moving from one location to another, such as across the internet or through a private enterprise network.

controls.title: 3.PEP.DO.DNMON
controls.description: Domain name monitoring allows agencies to discover the creation of or changes to agency domains.

controls.title: 3.PEP.DO.DNSIN
controls.description: Domain name sinkholing protections are a form of denylisting that protect clients from accessing malicious domains by responding to DNS queries for those domains.

controls.title: 3.PEP.DO.DNVAC
controls.description: Domain name verification protections ensure that domain name lookups from agency clients, whether for internal or external domains, are validated according to Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC).

controls.title: 3.PEP.DO.DNVAD
controls.description: Domain name validation protections ensure that all agency domain names are secured using DNSSEC, enabling external entities to validate their resolution to the domain names.

controls.title: 3.PEP.DO.PDSER
controls.description: CISA’s Protective DNS Service is a shared service offering that provides domain name sinkholing protections.

controls.title: 3.PEP.EM.AEPRO
controls.description: Adaptive email protections involve employing risk- based analysis in the application and enforcement of email protections.

controls.title: 3.PEP.EM.APPRO
controls.description: Anti-phishing protections detect instances of phishing and prevent users from accessing them.

controls.title: 3.PEP.EM.ARCHA
controls.description: Authenticated received chain allows for an intermediary, like a mailing list or forwarding service, to sign its own authentication of the original email, allowing downstream entities to accept the intermediary’s authentication even if the email was changed.

controls.title: 3.PEP.EM.ASPRO
controls.description: Anti-spam protections detect and quarantine instances of spam.

controls.title: 3.PEP.EM.CFILT
controls.description: Content filtering protections detect the presence of unapproved content and facilitate its removal or denial of access.

controls.title: 3.PEP.EM.DLPRE
controls.description: DLP technologies detect instances of the exfiltration, either malicious or accidental, of agency data.

controls.title: 3.PEP.EM.DSOEM
controls.description: Domain signature protections facilitate the authentication of outgoing email by signing the emails and ensuring that external parties may validate the email signatures according to the DMARC email authentication protocol that is defined in RFC 7489.

controls.title: 3.PEP.EM.DSVIE
controls.description: Domain signature verification protections authenticate incoming email according to the Domain-based Message Authentication Reporting and Conformance (DMARC) email authentication protocol defined in Request for Comments (RFC) 74895F6.

controls.title: 3.PEP.EM.E3AEP
controls.description: EINSTEIN 3 Accelerated (E3A) is an intrusion prevention capability offered by NCPS, provided by CISA, that includes an email filtering security service.

controls.title: 3.PEP.EM.EETRA
controls.description: Email services are configured to use encrypted connections, when possible, for communications between clients and other email servers.

controls.title: 3.PEP.EM.ELABE
controls.description: Email labeling is the process of automatically tagging incoming or outgoing email to manage risk.

controls.title: 3.PEP.EM.EOEMA
controls.description: Email encryption protections allow for the encryption of outgoing emails, which limits the visibility of their contents to the intended recipients.

controls.title: 3.PEP.EM.LCTPR
controls.description: Link click-through protections ensure that when a link from an email is clicked, the requester is directed to a protection that verifies the security of the link destination before permitting access.

controls.title: 3.PEP.EM.MCQUE
controls.description: Mail content query enables search and discovery for email across agency mailboxes.

controls.title: 3.PEP.EM.MFPRO
controls.description: Malicious file protections detect malicious attachments files in emails and prevent users from accessing them.

controls.title: 3.PEP.EM.MLPRO
controls.description: Malicious link protections detect malicious links in emails and prevent users from accessing them.

controls.title: 3.PEP.EM.PDPRO
controls.description: Post-delivery protections apply updated email protections to already delivered emails, enabling quarantining and mitigation for emails in mailboxes.

controls.title: 3.PEP.EM.SDENY
controls.description: Sender denylisting protections prevent the reception of email from denylisted senders, domains, or email servers.

controls.title: 3.PEP.EM.UDSOE
controls.description: User digital signature protections enable users to digitally sign their emails, allowing external parties to authenticate the email’s sender and its contents.

controls.title: 3.PEP.EM.UTIPP
controls.description: User tipping capabilities enable users to report emails, attachments, or URLs they suspect to be phishing attempts, spam, or otherwise malicious.

controls.title: 3.PEP.EN.ACONT
controls.description: An application container is a virtualization approach in which applications are isolated to a known set of dependencies, access methods, and interfaces.

controls.title: 3.PEP.EN.CMONI
controls.description: Costs monitoring entails the monitoring of costs incurred by enterprise resources.

controls.title: 3.PEP.EN.RDACC
controls.description: Remote desktop access solutions provide a mechanism for connecting to and controlling a remote physical or virtual computer.

controls.title: 3.PEP.EN.SITDE
controls.description: Shadow information technology (IT) detection systems detect the presence of unauthorized software and systems in use by an agency.

controls.title: 3.PEP.EN.SOARE
controls.description: Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR) tools define, prioritize, and automate the response to security incidents.

controls.title: 3.PEP.EN.VPNET
controls.description: Virtual private network (VPN) solutions provide a secure communications mechanism between networks that may traverse across unprotected or public networks.

controls.title: 3.PEP.FI.AMALW
controls.description: Anti-malware protections detect the presence of malicious code and facilitate its quarantine or removal.

controls.title: 3.PEP.FI.CDREC
controls.description: Content disarm and reconstruction technology detects the presence of unapproved active content and facilitates its removal.

controls.title: 3.PEP.FI.DCHAM
controls.description: Detonation chambers facilitate the detection of malicious code using protected and isolated execution environments to analyze the files.

controls.title: 3.PEP.FI.DLPRE
controls.description: Data loss prevention (DLP) technologies detect instances of the exfiltration, either malicious or accidental, of agency data.

controls.title: 3.PEP.ID.AAUTH
controls.description: Adaptive authentication aligns the strength of the PR.AC user or entity authentication mechanisms to the level of risk associated with the requested authorization.

controls.title: 3.PEP.ID.BBASE
controls.description: Behavioral baselining is capturing information about user and entity behavior to enable dynamic threat discovery and facilitate vulnerability management.

controls.title: 3.PEP.ID.CAUTH
controls.description: Continuous authentication entails validating and re-authenticating identity through the lifecycle of entity interactions.

controls.title: 3.PEP.ID.EIAMA
controls.description: Enterprise ICAM entails maintaining visibility into agency identities across agency environments and managing changes to those identities through a formal (preferably automated) process.

controls.title: 3.PEP.ID.EINVE
controls.description: Entitlement inventory entails developing, documenting, and maintaining a current inventory of user and entity permissions and authorizations to agency resources.

controls.title: 3.PEP.ID.MAUTH
controls.description: MFA entails using two or more factors to verify user or entity identity.

controls.title: 3.PEP.ID.SIDEN
controls.description: Service identity ensures that users and entities can authenticate the identities of agency services.

controls.title: 3.PEP.ID.SMANA
controls.description: Secrets management entails developing and using a formal process to securely track and manage digital authentication credentials, including certificates, passwords, and API keys.

controls.title: 3.PEP.IN.AACON
controls.description: Adaptive access control technologies factor in additional context, like security risk, operational needs, and other heuristics, when evaluating access control decisions.

controls.title: 3.PEP.IN.CTLMO
controls.description: Certificate transparency log monitoring allows agencies to discover when new certificates are issued for agency domains.

controls.title: 3.PEP.IN.DPLAT
controls.description: Deception platform technologies provide decoy environments, from individual machines to entire networks, that can be used to deflect attacks away from the operational systems supporting agency missions/business functions.

controls.title: 3.PEP.IN.EDRES
controls.description: Endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools combine endpoint and network event data to aid in the detection of malicious activity.

controls.title: 3.PEP.IN.IDPSY
controls.description: Intrusion detection systems detect and report malicious activity. Intrusion prevention systems attempt to stop the activity.

controls.title: 3.PEP.IN.NDRES
controls.description: Network detection and response involves the collection and analysis of network event data to aid in the detection and remediation of malicious activity.

controls.title: 3.PEP.NE.ACONT
controls.description: Access control protections prevent the ingress, egress, or transmission of unauthorized network traffic.

controls.title: 3.PEP.NE.HCONT
controls.description: Host containment protections enable a network to revoke or quarantine a host’s access to the network.

controls.title: 3.PEP.NE.IADEN
controls.description: Internet address denylisting protections prevent the ingest or transiting of traffic received from or destined to a denylisted internet address.

controls.title: 3.PEP.NE.MICRO
controls.description: Microsegmentation divides the network, either physically or virtually, according to the communication needs of application and data workflows, facilitating security controls to protect the data.

controls.title: 3.PEP.NE.NSEGM
controls.description: Network segmentation separates a given network into subnetworks, facilitating security controls between the subnetworks, and decreasing the attack surface of the network.

controls.title: 3.PEP.NE.RCONT
controls.description: Resource containment protections enable removal or quarantine of a resource’s access to other resources.

controls.title: 3.PEP.RE.DDSPR
controls.description: Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) protections mitigate the effects of distributed denial of service attacks.

controls.title: 3.PEP.RE.EEXPS
controls.description: Elastic expansion enables agencies to dynamically expand the resources available for services as conditions require.

controls.title: 3.PEP.RE.RDELI
controls.description: Regional delivery technologies enable the deployment of agency services across geographically diverse locations.

controls.title: 3.PEP.SE.ACMIT
controls.description: Active content mitigation protections detect the presence of unapproved active content and facilitate its removal.

controls.title: 3.PEP.SE.ACONT
controls.description: Access control technologies allow an agency to define policies limiting what actions may be performed by connected users and entities.

controls.title: 3.PEP.SE.DLPRE
controls.description: DLP technologies detect instances of the exfiltration, either malicious or accidental, of agency data.

controls.title: 3.PEP.SE.MCFIL
controls.description: Malicious content filtering protections detect the presence of malicious content and facilitate its removal.

controls.title: 3.PEP.SE.PCENF
controls.description: Protocol compliance enforcement technologies ensure that traffic complies with protocol definitions, documented by the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF).

controls.title: 3.PEP.UN.APPRO
controls.description: Anti-phishing protections detect instances of phishing and prevent users from accessing them.

controls.title: 3.PEP.UN.CTERM
controls.description: Connection termination mechanisms ensure the meeting host can positively control participation through inactivity timeouts, on-demand prompts, unique access codes for each meeting, host participant eviction, and even meeting duration limits.

controls.title: 3.PEP.UN.DLPRE
controls.description: Mechanisms should be implemented to control the sharing of information between UCC participants, intentional or incidental. This may be integrated into additional agency DLP technologies and can include keyword matching, attachment file type or existence prohibitions, attachment size limitations, or even audio/visual filters.

controls.title: 3.PEP.UN.ECOMM
controls.description: Communication between virtual meeting participants and any data exchanged is encrypted at rest and in transit. Some UCC offerings support end-to-end encryption, where encryption is performed on the clients and can only be decrypted by the other authenticated participants and cannot be decrypted by the UCC vendor.

controls.title: 3.PEP.UN.IVERI
controls.description: Identity verification ensures that access to the virtual meeting is limited to appropriate individuals. Waiting room features, where the meeting host authorizes vetted individuals to join the meeting, can also be utilized.

controls.title: 3.PEP.UN.LCTPR
controls.description: Link click-through protections ensure that when a link in communications is clicked, the requester is directed to a protection that verifies the security of the link destination before permitting access.

controls.title: 3.PEP.UN.MFPRO
controls.description: Malicious file protections detect malicious files in communications and prevent users from accessing them.

controls.title: 3.PEP.UN.MLPRO
controls.description: Malicious link protections detect malicious links in communications and prevent users from accessing them.

controls.title: 3.PEP.WE.ACMIT
controls.description: Active content mitigation protections detect the presence of unapproved active content and facilitate its removal.

controls.title: 3.PEP.WE.ACONT
controls.description: Access control technologies allow an agency to define policies limiting what actions may be performed by connected users and entities.

controls.title: 3.PEP.WE.APROX
controls.description: Authenticated proxies require entities to authenticate with the proxy before making use of it, enabling user, group, and location-aware security controls.

controls.title: 3.PEP.WE.BCONT
controls.description: Bandwidth control technologies allow for limiting the amount of bandwidth used by different classes of domains.

controls.title: 3.PEP.WE.BINSP
controls.description: Break and Inspect systems, or encryption proxies, terminate encrypted traffic, logging or performing policy enforcement against the plaintext, and re- encrypting the traffic, if applicable, before transmitting to the final destination.

controls.title: 3.PEP.WE.CDENY
controls.description: Certificate denylisting protections prevent communication with entities that use a set of known bad certificates.

controls.title: 3.PEP.WE.CFILT
controls.description: Content filtering protections detect the presence of unapproved content and facilitate its removal or denial of access.

controls.title: 3.PEP.WE.DCFIL
controls.description: Domain category filtering technologies allow for classes of domains (e.g., banking, medical) to receive a different set of security protections.

controls.title: 3.PEP.WE.DLPRE
controls.description: DLP technologies detect instances of the exfiltration, either malicious or accidental, of agency data.

controls.title: 3.PEP.WE.DREPF
controls.description: Domain reputation filtering protections are a form of domain denylisting based on a domain’s reputation, as defined by either the agency or an external entity.

controls.title: 3.PEP.WE.DRESF
controls.description: Domain resolution filtering prevents entities from using unauthorized DNS resolution services over the DNS-over-Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure (HTTPS) domain resolution protocol.

controls.title: 3.PEP.WE.MCFIL
controls.description: Malicious content filtering protections detect the presence of malicious content and facilitate its removal.

controls.title: 3.PEP.WE.PCENF
controls.description: Protocol compliance enforcement technologies ensure that traffic complies with protocol definitions, documented by the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF).

controls.title: 3.UNI.AACCO
controls.description: Auditing and accounting includes capturing business records (e.g., logs and other telemetry), making them available for auditing and accounting as required, and designing an auditing system that considers insider threat (e.g., separation of duties violation tracking) such that insider abuse or misuse can be detected.

controls.title: 3.UNI.BRECO
controls.description: Backup and recovery entails keeping copies of configuration and data, as needed, to allow for the quick restoration of service in the event of malicious incidents, system failures, or corruption.

controls.title: 3.UNI.CLMAN
controls.description: Central log management with analysis is the collection, storage, and analysis of telemetry, where the collection and storage are designed to facilitate data fusion and where the security analysis aids in discovery and response to malicious activity.

controls.title: 3.UNI.CMANA
controls.description: Configuration management is the implementation of a formal plan for documenting and managing changes to the environment, and monitoring for deviations, preferably automated.

controls.title: 3.UNI.DTDIS
controls.description: Dynamic threat discovery is the practice of using dynamic approaches (e.g., heuristics, baselining, etc.) to discover new malicious activity.

controls.title: 3.UNI.ETINT
controls.description: Enterprise threat intelligence is the usage of threat intelligence from private or government sources to implement mitigations for the identified risks.

controls.title: 3.UNI.EUSSE
controls.description: Effective use of shared services means that shared services are employed, where applicable, and individually tailored and measured to independently validate service conformance, and offer effective protections for tenants against malicious actors, both external and internal to the service provider.

controls.title: 3.UNI.IDMRP
controls.description: This entails the definition and enforcement of policies that apply to a given agency entity independent of its location.

controls.title: 3.UNI.INVENT
controls.description: Inventory entails developing, documenting, and maintaining a current inventory of all systems, networks, and components so that only authorized devices are given access, and unauthorized and unmanaged devices are found and restricted from gaining access.

controls.title: 3.UNI.IRPIH
controls.description: Incident response planning and incident handling is the documentation and implementation of a set of instructions, procedures, or technical capabilities to sense and detect, respond to, limit consequences of malicious cyberattacks, and restore the integrity of the network and associated systems.

controls.title: 3.UNI.LPRIV
controls.description: Least privilege is a design principle whereby each entity is granted the minimum system resources and authorizations that the entity needs to perform its function.

controls.title: 3.UNI.PEPAR
controls.description: Policy enforcement parity entails consistently applying security protections and other policies, independent of the communication mechanism, forwarding path, or endpoints used.

controls.title: 3.UNI.PMANA
controls.description: Patch management is the identification, acquisition, installation, and verification of patches for products and systems.

controls.title: 3.UNI.RESIL
controls.description: Resilience entails ensuring that systems, services, and protections maintain acceptable performance under adverse conditions.

controls.title: 3.UNI.SADMI
controls.description: Secure administration entails performing administrative tasks in a secure manner, using secure protocols.

controls.title: 3.UNI.SAUTH
controls.description: Strong authentication verifies the identity of users, devices, or other entities through rigorous means (e.g., multi-factor authentication) before granting access.

controls.title: 3.UNI.SAWAR
controls.description: Situational awareness is maintaining effective awareness, both current and historical, across all components.

controls.title: 3.UNI.TSYNC
controls.description: Time synchronization is the coordination of system (e.g., servers, workstations, network devices) clocks to minimize the difference between system clock times and enable accurate comparison of timestamps between systems.

controls.title: 3.UNI.UATRA
controls.description: User awareness and training entails that all users are informed of their roles and responsibilities and appropriate cybersecurity education is provisioned to enable users to perform their duties in a secure manner.

controls.title: 3.UNI.VMANG
controls.description: Vulnerability management is the practice of proactively working to discover vulnerabilities by including the use of both active and passive means of discovery and by taking action to mitigate discovered vulnerabilities.

controls.title: 3.UNL.CMREP
controls.description: Continuous monitoring reporting entails the maintenance of ongoing awareness of informational security, vulnerabilities, and threats to support organizational risk management decisions.

controls.title: 3.UNL.GPAUD
controls.description: Governance and policy auditing entails validating the proper definition, application, and enforcement of agency rules and policies.

controls.title: 3.UNL.RLMAN
controls.description: Resource lifecycle management is the end-to-end process of managing resources from development to operation to retirement, such that resources are provisioned and decommissioned in conjunction with the applications they support.

controls.title: 3.UNL.STEXE
controls.description: Security tests (e.g., penetration testing or red teaming) verify the extent to which a system resists active attempts to compromise its security. Security exercises are simulations of emergencies that validate and identify gaps in plans and procedures.
